text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: cluster-us-west-2: pod/redwood-runtime-zzzz OOM killed during prefill loop (GPU0). Auto-restart triggered. Visible error: CUDA out of memory while allocating 1.25 GiB. Investigating.

sre-lucy: digging in now, looking at node telemetry and container logs.

ml-oncall-raj: I’m on call — taking it. Any customer impact noted yet?

se-chris: We started seeing 5xx spikes on /v1/generate for a handful of large-context customers ~3m ago. Error rate ~12% for that route.

infra-miguel: Node k8s-node-7 reported a kernel OOM kill then kubelet restarted the pod. GPU memory across node looks saturated — long-context prefill tasks pushing seq length ~120k tokens.

ml-oncall-raj: Can you paste the relevant logs? I want the CUDA stack and the model variant.

sre-lucy: pasted snippet from pod logs:
```
2026-03-17T10:02:04Z runtime: allocate(KVCache) size=1258291200
E CUDA OOM: out of memory trying to allocate 1258291200 bytes
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runtime/prefill.py", line 212, in run_prefill
    kv_cache.alloc(batch_id)
RuntimeError: CudaOutOfMemoryError: failed to allocate
```
Model: open-llama-xl-32k (quantized int8) on gpu:0

ml-oncall-raj: Thanks. Two immediate mitigations: 1) enable prefill-trimming to cap prefix to 32k tokens for in-flight requests, 2) route heavy requests to fallback model open-llama-7b that fits in smaller GPU memory pool.

sre-lucy: Can we enable trimming via config safely? How quick is the rollout?

ml-oncall-raj: Yes, patching runtime config now. Command:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/redwood-runtime PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=32768
```
Rolling update will start in ~30s.

infra-miguel: Also temporarily scaling up Dedicated pool by 2 nodes (g5x2) to reduce contention. K8s autoscaler bumped but manual scale to expedite.

se-chris: Client-facing note: for customers with long-history prompts we’ll trim older messages to avoid sudden truncation surprises. CS should pre-warn.

cs-amy: noted. I’ll draft a short message for affected customers: "We observed transient errors for very large-context requests and have applied mitigations. If you experience truncation, contact support." Send me the exact affected tenant ids.

sre-lucy: Affected tenants: tenant-842, tenant-199, tenant-7 (high-volume long-context). I’ll send a list via DM.

ml-oncall-raj: After config patch, observing fewer OOMs. Still seeing 1 pod restart every 10m on that node — looks like noisy neighbor long-lived KV cache not evicting properly.

sre-lucy: Enabling aggressive KV eviction policy:
```
PATCH /api/v1/runtime/config
{
  "kv_cache": {"eviction_threshold":"0.65", "on_prefill_eviction":"trim_oldest"}
}
```
Applied.

infra-miguel: Node k8s-node-7 still showing flappy behavior; I’m cordoning node and draining non-critical pods to isolate. Scheduling new runtime pods onto node-3 and node-4.

ml-oncall-raj: Good. Also adding a routing rule to prefer quantized-7b fallback for requests with >30k window until we finish root cause.

sre-lucy: Monitoring metrics: error rate dropped to ~1.8% on /v1/generate in 4m. Latency slightly increased for routed requests but overall stable.

se-chris: Any sign this is a kernel-driver issue vs just memory pressure from large requests?

infra-miguel: No driver traces indicating reset; it's pure allocation failures. Kernel OOM was due to GPU mem pressure cascading. I’ll keep node cordoned until we confirm.

ml-oncall-raj: Next steps: 1) collect full heapdump from affected pod for postmortem, 2) add testcase to repro with 100k token prompt, 3) evaluate dynamic prefix compression to avoid KV growth.

sre-lucy: I’ll file the incident ticket with timeline and mitigations. Starting postmortem stub now.

cs-amy: Sent the customer note to affected tenants, included our mitigation and ETA for follow-up. Marking as "limited impact" but will escalate if recurrence.

ml-oncall-raj: Handoff to morning oncall: @sre-lucy and @infra-miguel will continue next steps. If OOMs spike again, re-open page.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=sev2 -> mitigated. Actions: PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=32768, KV eviction tightened, node-7 cordoned, fallback routing enabled.

sre-lucy: Quick summary for handoff: cause=GPU OOMs during prefill from extreme long-context requests; mitigations applied=trim prefix, evict KV aggressively, route >30k to smaller model, cordon node. Follow-ups=heapdump analysis, repro test, consider server-side prefix compression + rate-limits on extremely long requests.

ml-oncall-raj: Thanks team. I’ll attach logs and heapdump to the ticket. Paging silence in 30m if stable.

cs-amy: I’ll follow up with customers once we have root-cause. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
